title: 49ers receiver Pearsall undergoes knee surgery, eyes 2027 return
dek: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Ricky Pearsall underwent right knee surgery to repair his posterior cruciate ligament and is targeting a nine-month recovery timeline, per ESPN. If the recovery goes as planned, he could return for the start of the 2027 season.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Ricky Pearsall had PCL surgery and is targeting a nine-month recovery, aiming to return in 2027.
bottom_line: Pearsall's recovery path will shape whether the 49ers commit to a fifth-year extension and whether he returns to the form projected when drafted. Watch for any updates on rehabilitation progress and the team's formal stance on keeping him through 2027.
body: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Ricky Pearsall underwent surgery to repair the posterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and is targeting roughly a nine-month recovery before returning to the field, according to ESPN.

If the recovery proceeds as expected, Pearsall could be ready for the start of the 2027 season, per ESPN's reporting. The timeline marks a second significant injury obstacle for the receiver in his three-year career.

Pearsall initially injured the knee in a Week 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, an injury that cost him all or parts of 10 games. The 49ers and Pearsall opted against surgery in the offseason in hopes that rehab and rest would allow him to return to full strength. However, after just three training camp practices this year, Pearsall experienced swelling in the knee. The team placed him on season-ending injured reserve nearly two weeks ago.

Pearsall has played only 20 games in three seasons despite never missing a game at the University of Florida. He carries 67 receptions for 928 yards and three touchdowns for his career. In his rookie year, he missed the first six games after being shot in an attempted robbery in San Francisco.

The 49ers will have to decide on the fifth-year option with Pearsall next offseason. In an Instagram post after the surgery, Pearsall said he had "no regrets" and "no what ifs," noting that he had "nothing to be disappointed about" knowing that "I did everything I could." He also wrote: "Now it's time. Time to completely shift my mind. Time to hone in on every aspect of myself mentally, physically and spiritually. Time to lock it all in... The road back starts now. I'm ready for every part of it."
